sections.label: Requisition of Resources Act 1985
sections.summary: The 1985 Requisition of Resources Act allows requisition of essential civil resources for public safety, defence, essential supplies and services, or exercises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: The Requisition of Resources Act passed by Parliament in 1985 provided for the requisition of essential civil resources from individuals, businesses and organisations when it is "necessary for the securing of the public safety and defence of the country; or for the maintenance of supplies and services essential to the life of the community; or for the conduct of exercises for any of the aforesaid purposes".

sections.label: Servicemen acknowledge notices electronically
sections.summary: About 75% of servicemen acknowledge receipt of notices and orders electronically by the first or second SMS without hardcopy reminders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Around 75% of our servicemen today acknowledge receipt of their notices and orders electronically by the first or second SMS and do not need to receive hardcopy reminders.

sections.label: Consent for electronic orders
sections.summary: A proposed section 30(2A) requires consent before orders and notices sent electronically can be presumed received and read.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Third, as an added safeguard, we have proposed a new provision at section 30(2A), which requires consent to be given before orders and notices sent by electronic means can be presumed and deemed to have been received and read.

sections.label: Exit Permit strict liability clarified
sections.summary: Section 32 of the amended Enlistment Act states NS-liable persons from age 13 must meet Exit Permit requirements even without NS registration or Registration Notice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: There had been past offenders who have claimed that they were not liable for Exit Permit offences just because they had not received a Registration Notice for NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: So, in order to make clear the intent of the law as it stands, section 32 of the amended Enlistment Act will now state explicitly that all NS-liable persons from age 13 onwards must adhere to Exit Permit requirements even if they have not yet registered for NS or have not yet received their Registration Notice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: The amendment will clarify our existing policy and legal position which is that Exit Permit offences are strict liability in nature, that is, a person cannot claim to not be liable simply because he claims to be ignorant of the law of his NS obligations.

sections.label: Periods not counting towards NS
sections.summary: The amendment clarifies periods of absence that do not count towards NS liabilities, including disciplinary imprisonment, pre-trial custody, and rescinded medical leave.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: The amendment will make clear the periods of time where the serviceman's absence from service will not count towards the fulfilment of his NS liabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: This will include periods of absence due to disciplinary reasons, for example, local and overseas imprisonment or detention; pre-trial civil custody for offences that the serviceman is subsequently convicted of; and rescinded medical leave, such as when a serviceman is found to have abused his medical leave when he was actually fit for duty.

sections.label: Full-time NS liability duration
sections.summary: Statutory full-time NS liability remains up to two-and-a-half years for those promoted above certain ranks, after last being reduced to two years in June 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even after amendments made in section 4 of the Bill, the statutory full-time NS liability remains at up to two-and-a-half years for anyone promoted above the rank of Lance Corporal in the SAF or SCDF, or Special Constable 2 in the SPF, which, in practice, covers every enlistee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The duration of full-time NS was last reduced from two-and-a-half years to two years in June 2004.

sections.label: NS liability length question
sections.summary: Asks why the Bill does not amend full-time NS liability from two-and-a-half to two years, a practice for 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, if yes, why has the Bill we are debating today not included an amendment to reduce the statutory length of full-time NS liability from two-and-a-half to two years, even though this has been the practice for 20 years, which is practically one generation?

sections.label: Section 12 service extension
sections.summary: Proposed changes to section 12 on full-time service liability in SPF and SCDF raise questions about service extension for specific ranks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed changes to section 12 regarding liability to render full-time service, particularly in the SPF and SCDF, raise questions about service extension for specific ranks.

sections.label: Section 37 oversight request
sections.summary: Urges the Minister to address amendments to section 37 and clarify regulation-making powers, citing oversight and public scrutiny as safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Robust Parliamentary oversight and public scrutiny are essential safeguards against potential misuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Minister to address the proposed amendments to section 37 of the Act pursuant to clause 12 of the Bill and clarify the Minister's regulation-making powers.

sections.label: Digital battlefield foreign adversaries
sections.summary: Foreign adversaries use algorithms and misinformation to manipulate public opinion and sow discord, paving the way for real-world conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the silent trenches of the digital battlefield, foreign adversaries weaponise algorithms and misinformation, manipulating public opinion and sowing discord, paving the way for real-world conflict with every unseen click.

sections.label: Clause 9 electronic notices
sections.summary: Urges the House to consider points on the Bill, focusing on clause 9 allowing service of notices by SMS, email and NS Portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This framework will not only safeguard our nation through military might, but also through the unity and unwavering spirit of every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the House to carefully consider these points as we move forward with this important Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us work together to ensure that our National Service system remains effective, inclusive and responsive to the evolving needs of our nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One area I would like to focus on is clause 9, which amends section 30 of the Enlistment Act to allow service of notices by SMS, email and an electronic service platform, which I understand is the NS Portal.

sections.label: Contact details and call-up notice
sections.summary: Phone numbers and emails may change, so a person could be charged for missing a call-up deemed received at his last contact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is likely that phone numbers and email addresses may change over time and they may overlook updating MINDEF of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This would mean it is possible for that person to get charged for not attending a call-up because under the amended legislation, he could be deemed to have received notice when the SMS or email is sent to his last contact number even though the person did not, in fact, get the call-up notice.

sections.label: Registered post follow-up practice
sections.summary: MINDEF follows up with registered post to confirm receipt, and will continue conventional notice if electronic call-up is not acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The current practice of following up with the registered post is helpful because MINDEF knows for sure whether or not the person has actually received the notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I note that Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How has given significant assurances on this that MINDEF will continue its practice of following up with the conventional notice in the event the electronic call-up notice is not acknowledged for any reason.

sections.label: Convenience for NSmen
sections.summary: Electronic means aim to enhance convenience for NSmen, and 75% already acknowledge orders and notices by SMS reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Rather, it is to enhance the convenience accorded to our NSmen, in being properly informed though means that most are very comfortable with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: And as I mentioned earlier, 75% of NSmen already are acknowledging these orders and notices by replying to the SMS.

sections.label: Consent for electronic notices
sections.summary: The proposed legislation requires consent before electronic orders and notices can be presumed received and read.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The proposed legislation also requires consent to be given before orders and notices sent by electronic means can be presumed and deemed to have been received and read.

sections.label: Section 12 amendments and NS duration
sections.summary: Amendments to section 12 do not affect full-time NS duration, maintained at two years for all NS-liable individuals regardless of rank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: In reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng, the amendments to section 12 do not impact the duration of full-time NS, which is maintained at two years for all NS-liable individuals regardless of rank.

sections.label: Reduced effective NS period
sections.summary: In June 2004 the effective NS period was reduced from two-and-a-half years to two years, still the case today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: And if through technology, better processes, productivity improvements, you can require less time from the people so that they can pursue other important priorities in their lives, then, you should do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: This was exactly why, as Mr Leong Mun Wai pointed out, in June 2004, the effective NS period was reduced from two-and-a-half years to two years, which is still the case today, notwithstanding that maximum.

sections.label: Self-employed NSmen income data
sections.summary: With consent, self-employed NSmen income data is retrieved from IRAS and MUP recalculated from latest income Notice of Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: For most self-employed NSmen, with their consent, the income data is retrieved from IRAS and their MUP is automatically re-calculated based on the average monthly trade income in their latest income Notice of Assessment.

sections.label: Volunteer ex-NSmen protections
sections.summary: Section 68A of the Police Force Act and section 9A of the Civil Defence Act give SPF and SCDF volunteer ex-NSmen the same protections as Part 6 of the Enlistment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: For SPF and SCDF volunteer ex-NSmen, section 68A of the Police Force Act and section 9A of the Civil Defence Act already accord them the same protections as Part 6 of the Enlistment Act.

sections.label: Regulations and primary legislation
sections.summary: Regulations are subsidiary legislation that must stay within the Enlistment Act's scope, and Act-level amendments go through parliamentary processes with oversight and public scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: As Members know, the Regulations are subsidiary legislation and subsidiary legislation must conform to and cannot fall outside of the scope of the overriding primary legislation, and the Enlistment Act is the primary legislation in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: So, when you make Regulations pursuant to this Act, it must keep within the scope of the mother Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: And all amendments at the Act level will need to go through the relevant parliamentary processes, where they will be subject to parliamentary oversight and public scrutiny.

sections.label: Requisition systems amendments and sitting suspension
sections.summary: The proposed amendments keep NS and civil resources requisition systems effective and up-to-date; the Sitting was suspended until 3.30 pm for the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will ensure that our NS and civil resources requisition systems keep up with the times and remain effective and up-to-date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance is due to give his Budget Statement at 3.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, we do have some time and we will all have a longer break.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and I will take the Chair at 3.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 1.36 pm until 3.30 pm.
